ranked.title: The lattice crossing exponent E(m) vs m: a decisive test for interval and lattice factor bases
ranked.surface: 2(a) interval/lattice-defined factor bases + 2(c) lattice (not Groebner) solving
ranked.one_line: Measure the largest box exponent e* at which a Jochemsz-May shift lattice recovers a planted Semaev relation, against the e >= 1/m that relation existence demands.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The integer lift of S_{m+1} (tiny coefficients: 1,2,4,28 for S_3) plus the archimedean/metric structure of Z; the lattice acts on coefficient vectors of a fixed integer polynomial, an object a generic group has no access to.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Highest information per unit cost left in the program. The naive-lattice half is already done and validated (e* ~ 0.11 = 1/E(2) at 32/40/48 bits; closed form E(m)=2^{m-2}(2^{m-1}+1)(2m-1) = 9,50,252,1224,6076 proved, so E(m)>m for all m). The one-hour residual is the only experiment that closes a whole branch (every interval/GAP/box/Eisenstein/digit factor base attacked by lattices) rather than one idea, and it carries a pre-registered falsifiable prediction.
ranked.first_experiment: Rerun the planted-solution harness at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-virtualaquarium/e2bf485c-5536-57b5-8ef5-8e69bb3bcc7b/scratchpad/lat.py with a real Jochemsz-May shift lattice for f(x1,x2)=S_3(x1,x2,x_R) mod p (shifts x1^i x2^j f^k to k=2,3, dimension 15-35, fplll/fpylll or exact LLL), on y^2=x^3+7 over 32/40/48-bit primes of prime order; plant x_R = x(P1+P2) with x1,x2 in the box; binary-search e* = max log_p(prod X_i) at which recovery succeeds, 25 instances per cell. Log as a by-product the empirical decomposition count H^m/p at 40 bits.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if e* saturates below 0.5 as shift order grows (prediction: 0.20-0.25). ESCALATE only if e* trends toward or past 0.5 — and first audit the planting, since x_R accidentally revealing x1+x2 is the obvious bug that would fake it.
ranked.audit_flag: Existence and solvability are exactly complementary at every m with zero margin: relations exist only for e >= 1/m, and any Coppersmith-type method needs the root count polynomially bounded, i.e. e < 1/m.

ranked.title: Relation search as a low-weight-codeword problem: Riemann-Roch evaluation vectors, Plucker collisions, and ISD
ranked.surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves (relations from divisors of low-degree functions)
ranked.one_line: Measure total-work-per-relation across an (N, m) grid to test the scale-free invariant that prime-field elliptic index calculus costs ~p regardless of factor-base size or decomposition length.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Explicit F_p coordinates: v(P)=(1,x,y,x^2,xy,...) makes the parity-check matrix computable without knowing any discrete log (verified 11987/11987 agreement between singularity of the m x m evaluation matrix and 'the m points sum to O').
ranked.why_ranked_here: The single most reusable number in the whole program: p/N per relation, total ~p independent of N and m, is the accounting invariant that decides torus-dickson, semaev-skew, sparse-limb, snfs-order, eisenstein-residue, interval-factor-base and batch-economics simultaneously. Half a day of hash-table code, no exotic tooling, and the only outcome that resurrects a dozen ideas at once is a cell where total work falls materially below p.
ranked.first_experiment: C or Python+gmpy2 on y^2=x^3+7 over p = 1 mod 3 with prime order, 20-40 bits. (a) For m in {3,4,5} and N spanning 2^4..2^12, enumerate (m-1)-subsets of the factor base, hash-lookup the negated sum, count actual relations, report total work per relation. (b) Implement Prange and Stern over F_p on the explicit m x N evaluation matrix and measure per-iteration success directly against the prediction m!/N^{m-1}. (c) Instrument (no algorithm) the Plucker half-support list sizes C(N,m/2) and the orthogonal-pair count ~L^2/p.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if (a) reproduces total work ~p in every cell and (b) gives Prange success = m!/N^{m-1}. ALIVE only if some (N,m) cell shows total work materially below p — that would falsify the framing all downstream ideas rest on.
ranked.audit_flag: The Plucker meet-in-the-middle costs N^m, a factor N worse than the N^{m-1} textbook baseline; and at weight = redundancy = m with rate -> 1, ISD is provably worse than brute force.

ranked.title: Positive-control calibration: do coordinate-level distinguishers have ANY power, measured against planted bias?
ranked.surface: Measurement methodology: false-negative rates for statistical distinguishers on DL tables
ranked.one_line: Measure the minimum detectable effect of every distinguisher in the program by planting a bias of known magnitude in an AES-encoded group, then run the same battery on j=0 with all known symmetries quotiented out.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The test arm feeds real F_p coordinate features (cubic character, limb boxes, Hamming weight) and secp256k1's own structure (j=0 CM, free lambda, pseudo-Mersenne limbs) into detectors that an opaque encoding cannot even define.
ranked.why_ranked_here: This is the missing control arm for roughly a third of the queue (fourier-heavy-hunt, p-shape-distinguisher, cm-height-oracle, detectable-difference-set, preprocessing-advice, dl-free-homomorphy, multiplicative-coset). Without a measured MDE every null in that family is uninformative. One day, and it converts a pile of shrugs into one calibrated number per detector. Ranked below the two cheaper items only on cost.
ranked.first_experiment: Replace the proposed broken-curve positive controls with PLANTED bias: on Z/n under an AES bijection, reveal a chosen linear functional of k in a chosen coordinate bit with probability eps; sweep eps down and bit size 20->26 up; report per-detector ROC and the smallest eps detected at 5% FPR. Separately pre-register the known j=0 positives (chi_3(beta*x)=chi_3(x)+1 mod 3 exactly, verified 2000/2000 at p=1048783; the 3-fold lambda permutation; negation) and run every j=0 detector on lambda-orbit- and negation-quotiented data.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD-FOR-THE-PROGRAM if every detector's MDE tracks 1/sqrt(n) — detection power then buys nothing a birthday bound does not, and all bias-hunting nulls are confirmed uninformative-but-unnecessary. DEAD-FOR-SECP256K1 if, after quotienting, j=0 z-scores are indistinguishable from random-j at every size.
ranked.audit_flag: The originally proposed positive controls (anomalous, small-k) are known-ATTACKABLE, not known-BIASED — their attacks are an exact p-adic isomorphism and an exact pairing, neither of which predicts any statistical anomaly, so the power curve as designed would be vacuous.

ranked.title: Hunting a computable proxy for the Z[omega]-norm: a 4-query reduction from ECDLP to any height oracle
ranked.surface: Coordinate statistics vs the GLV/CM height on E(F_p)
ranked.one_line: Measure the oracle-quality THRESHOLD, not the correlation: plot the minimum Pearson eps at which the monic-quadratic fit recovers 2a-b exactly, as a function of n.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The F_p coordinate encoding (integer size, rational reconstruction, characters) against the canonical short Z[omega] representative; the CM lattice makes a height exist, and the question is purely whether the encoding leaks lattice position.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Kills an entire family — every 'partial/noisy oracle for a hidden quantity' proposal — by extrapolation rather than by fishing, and it is ~80% already built (scripts in scratchpad/audit/). The measured 1-eps_crit ~ n^{-1/2} law plus the Voronoi cap W = O(sqrt n) together show the reduction needs an essentially exact oracle, which is the sharpest quantitative form of the 'no computable height' folklore.
ranked.first_experiment: Synthesize s = N(alpha) + noise with tunable Pearson eps; run the least-squares monic-quadratic fit; plot minimum eps for EXACT recovery of 2a-b at 20/28/36/44 bits; test the prediction 1-eps_crit ~ n^{-1/2}. Alongside, log the Voronoi piece-length scaling (median second-difference run length / sqrt n; measured 0.42 at n=2^20) to confirm W is capped at O(sqrt n). Build DL tables by walking P = P+G so every log is known by construction (removes the 2^32 ceiling).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if 1-eps_crit ~ n^{-1/2} holds across four sizes (implying eps within 2^-128 of 1 at 256 bits) and the Voronoi run-length ratio is constant. Also DEAD if end-to-end exact recovery from any real statistic fails at 20 bits — it already does.
ranked.audit_flag: The proposed oracle is DLP-complete: h(Q)-h(Q-G)+1 = 2a-b recovers the full logarithm in O(1) group operations, so N(alpha) is a bijective repackaging of the discrete log, not an independent height.

ranked.title: Descent along p = t^8 - t - 977 (t = 2^32): carry-free Weil restriction to Z
ranked.surface: 2(e) the special shape of p: F_p as Z[T]/(T^8-T-977) at T = 2^32
ranked.one_line: Count exact integer solutions of S_3 = 0 in a box of side X and confirm the count is constant in X, i.e. the carry-free regime contains no relations at any p.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The SNFS representation p = f(2^32) with f sparse and tiny-height, so mod-p reduction is a shift-and-add; the factor base is defined by the base-t digit expansion of x.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Thirty seconds of work for a kill template that applies to the whole 'lift to Z / exploit the shape of p' family (sparse-limb, snfs-order, eisenstein-residue, surface-section, mw-lift). It replaces a density heuristic with a global-arithmetic finiteness statement, and its companion measurement proves the SNFS shape is formally inert.
ranked.first_experiment: A (30 s, no curve, no prime): for X in {64,256,1024,4096} loop over integer pairs |x1|,|x2| <= X, solve S_3(x1,x2,X3) as a quadratic in X3, count exact integer roots with |x3| <= X. Measured: N(X) = 3 at X=64,256,1024, all degenerate. B (1 min): for representations p = t^k - t - c with k = 2,4,8 at matched p, measure the carry-free digit bound B*(t,k,c) and the resulting factor base (2B*)^k; predicted identical exponent p^{1/deg S} across k.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if N(X) does not grow like X^2 (the heuristic count a useful factor base needs) — it is constant at 3. DEAD if B confirms the k-independence law, since the SNFS shape then contributes literally nothing over a trivial height bound.
ranked.audit_flag: Carry-freeness is logically equivalent to S_m = 0 over Z, i.e. an exact global relation among bounded-height lifts — Siegel/Mordell finiteness, which is the xedni failure mode in different clothing.

ranked.title: Homomorphy-defect maximization over coordinate circuits, with exact spectra and a 2-torsion positive control
ranked.surface: Approximate homomorphisms E(F_p) -> A from the explicit addition formulas
ranked.one_line: Build an exact-FFT harness that reports max_{c != 0}|ghat(c)| (mean projected out) for any coordinate predicate, fit its exponent, and calibrate against a curve where the predicate is an exact homomorphism.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Multiplicative/additive characters of low-degree polynomials in (x, y, beta*x) and limb slices of the canonical representative — objects defined by the field representation, with the addition formulas supplying the defect.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Thirty minutes for a reusable instrument that retires the whole coordinate-predicate family at once, with a genuine positive control (y^2 = x^3+3x^2+5x over F_10007 gives Pr = 1.0000 exactly, eps = 1/2) so that a null is interpretable rather than a shrug. Exact spectra remove optimizer overfitting, which is the failure mode that would otherwise manufacture a false positive.
ranked.first_experiment: Walk k -> kG for k = 0..N-1 in C, store f(kG) as one byte, take one real FFT of length N. Report max_{c!=0}|ghat(c)| / sqrt(N) for f in {chi(x), chi(g(x)) for random deg<=4 g, chi_3(x), LSB(x), MSB(x), limb slices}, at N = 2143, 8293, 32497, 130579, 524269, against a matched random +-1 control (measured 0.459) and a matched AES-encoded control. Fit alpha in max|ghat|/N ~ N^{-alpha}.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if alpha for every family equals the random control's alpha within noise across five sizes (measured so far: chi(x) 0.497, chi(deg-4) 0.464, LSB 0.440, MSB 0.466, best-of-200 0.476 vs random 0.459). ALIVE only if the ratio to the matched control GROWS with N. Never use eps or an absolute alpha threshold.
ranked.audit_flag: eps as literally defined is maximized to 1/2 by degenerate f (g = a perfect square gives f == +1), and unbalanced f fake a signal entirely through the mean; Deligne pins the honest statistic at alpha = 1/2 for the whole algebraic circuit class.

ranked.title: S_4 as a rank-4 bilinear form: relation search is orthogonality search, and the sum-membership oracle
ranked.surface: 2(a) structured factor bases + 2(c) resultant/orthogonality strategy
ranked.one_line: Count GROUP OPERATIONS for honest m=3 relation gathering across four bit-sizes and confirm the exponent sits at 2/3 and stays there.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The exact identity S_4 = (<u,v>^2 - D(u)D(v))/4 (verified symbolically) plus the rationality of sqrt(disc) forced by x(P1+P2), x(P1-P2) both lying in F_p — a coordinate-level fact with no generic analogue.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Two hours to retire 'structured factor base over a prime field' with a number instead of an argument, and the decisive sumset dichotomy is already measured: interval-of-x gives |{x(P+-P')}|/|B|^2 = 0.976, random 0.983, multiples-of-G 0.020. Coordinate-structured B has full sumset (no incidence to exploit); group-structured B collapses but is then a knapsack in Z/n where Shoup applies. Both branches dead, but the exponent plot is the reusable artifact.
ranked.first_experiment: On 24/28/32/36-bit curves, implement m=3 relation gathering honestly: precompute the sorted table of x(P2 +- P3) over B x B, then for each random R sort x(R +- P1) against it. Count group operations, not wall clock. Plot log(ops)/log(p) against the rho baseline sqrt(pi*n/4) on the same curves.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if the exponent sits at 2/3 across all four sizes. Skip the proposed degree-<=6 vanishing-ideal fit (it returns the known ideal of the 2-dimensional image surface) and the sort-vs-pairs timing (that IS the birthday bound, not a win).
ranked.audit_flag: The stated success condition is arithmetically empty: (2+delta)/3 < 1/2 needs delta < -1/2, so even a free perfect sum-membership oracle gives p^{2/3} = 2^170; and the rank-4 identity is specific to Res of two binary quadratics and does not extend to S_5.

ranked.title: Beating birthday needs a hash that detects a whole difference set, not just equality
ranked.surface: 8(h) coordinate LSH + 8(g) non-generic rho
ranked.one_line: Compute the EXACT autocorrelation A(k) of a coordinate hash along the full orbit x(jP0) for all shifts k <= 256, and test whether the conditional collision excess grows or decays with n.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The hash reads the coordinate representation (top bits, x mod small primes, character vectors, canonical-lift digits, Lattes-orbit minima); in the generic model conditional and unconditional collision rates are provably equal, so any excess is non-generic by construction.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Exhaustive enumeration of the whole orbit strictly dominates the proposed 10^7-pair sampling — it gives every t at once, at lower cost, with maximum statistical power. Partially run already: peak deviation falls 3.1x then 3.2x across n ratios 13.1 and 5.9, i.e. exactly the n^{-1/2} sampling floor, the opposite of the growth the idea itself declares necessary.
ranked.first_experiment: On y^2=x^3+7 with prime order at ~2^19, 2^22.7, 2^25.3 (and up to 2^26), enumerate the entire orbit x(jP0) and compute exact A(k) = #{j : h(x_j)=h(x_{j+k})} for all k <= 256 in one pass, against a shuffled control. Hash families: top-b bits, x mod small primes, character vectors, and — the two families NOT covered by Kohel-Shparlinski bounds — canonical-lift p-adic digits and Lattes/phi_2-orbit minima. Pre-register that only a fit r-1 ~ n^{+delta}, delta > 0, counts.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if r-1 decays like n^{-1/2} across five sizes (measured 0.0315 -> 0.0099 -> 0.0031) and the real curve's worst-z over 256 shifts is indistinguishable from the shuffled control's. Log max observed r as a permanent upper bound on what any hash of this type can buy.
ranked.audit_flag: At the strength the cost formula needs (r ~ |T| with range B = O(|T|)), the hypothesis is equivalent to predicting the top log2(n/|T|) bits of the discrete log with constant advantage — the premise is the conclusion.

ranked.title: Quantifying the height gap: exponentially many small lifts for F_p^* vs polynomially many for E
ranked.surface: 4(a)/4(e) what an elliptic SNFS would need, and the exact gap
ranked.one_line: Test whether the Mordell-Weil relation lattice under the Neron-Tate form is distinguishable from a random index-n sublattice with the same Gram.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Reduction E(K) -> E(F_p) at a degree-1 prime, Neron-Tate canonical heights, Mordell-Weil lattice geometry — relations would be found by lattice enumeration under a height quadratic form, invisible to a group oracle.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Converts the folklore 'reduction destroys height information' into a measured KS statistic, closing surface 4(a)/4(e) for good. The r=3 pilot is already run (real lambda_1/GH mean 1.128 sd 0.330 over 30 primes; random control 1.117 sd 0.316; two-sample t ~ 0.18) and the sweep to higher rank is hours.
ranked.first_experiment: Extend scratchpad/lat5.gp: sweep r = 3, 5, 8, 12 using small-generator curves from rank tables (and, for r >= 8, the multiquadratic-twist construction the idea itself proposes), p from 10 to 26 bits with #E(F_p) prime, ~200 primes per cell. Per cell record the full distribution of lambda_1/GH and the LLL-reduced Gram diagonal profile; compare to >= 2000 random index-n sublattices with the identical Gram via two-sample KS, not just means. Mechanics: qfminim throws on the scaled integer Gram; use the real Gram with qflllgram and read the reduced diagonal.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if the KS p-value exceeds 0.01 in every cell. Do NOT use the originally stated Poisson null — the relation set is a sublattice by construction, so a Poisson test is guaranteed to 'reject' and would read as a spurious positive.
ranked.audit_flag: To write down the relation lattice at all you must already know r discrete logs; without them the only membership test is one group operation per candidate, so the lattice is a costume over a generic search.

ranked.title: Measured hardness exponent of bit-level ECDLP encodings, with p-shape / lambda / ladder ablations
ranked.surface: 7a SAT/SMT bit-level encoding, treated as an instrument
ranked.one_line: Measure how many scalar bits must be fixed before unit propagation alone refutes a wrong prefix — a search-free probe that runs at 64 and even 256 bits.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The CNF sees the F_p multiplier and the pseudo-Mersenne reduction circuit (2^256 = 2^32 + 977 mod p), structure no generic algorithm can query.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The propagation-depth probe costs one propagation call per query, so unlike every previous SAT experiment it is not capped at toy sizes and produces a clean machine-independent number at the real curve. It settles the entire SAT/SMT surface (this idea plus sat-kangaroo-leakage-frontier) without any timeout extrapolation.
ranked.first_experiment: Build the CNF once per curve with a sound complete encoding — first fix the two bugs: use projective/Jacobian coordinates or an explicit exceptional-case disjunction so s*(x2-x1)=y2-y1 never silently forces UNSAT (measured degeneracy 9.1% at b=8, 2.9% at b=10), and hand-circuit pseudo-Mersenne reduction as shift+add+conditional-subtract instead of Z3's URem. For b = 12,16,20,24,32,48,64 and ~50 targets: flip one bit of the true k, assert the top L bits as assumptions in CaDiCaL/CryptoMiniSat via python-sat, and solve with a conflict budget of 0. Record the smallest refuting L vs b.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if refutation requires L = b (only a fully specified scalar is refutable), which forces c = 1 exactly and proves CDCL cannot beat enumerating its own backdoor. ALIVE only if refuting-L < b, and only then is the expensive exponent fit justified.
ranked.audit_flag: The pilot's measured c >= 1.1 is WORSE than scalar-bit enumeration (the b scalar bits are a strong backdoor, so complete CDCL is at worst 2^b poly) — reporting 1.1 as 'the exponent' would be a solver-heuristic pathology, not a property of the problem.

ranked.title: Machine-searched structured factor bases over F_p, judged against a counting bound and a measured solve cost
ranked.surface: 7c automated factor-base discovery + 7e measured decomposition cost
ranked.one_line: Measure the degree of regularity of the RESTRICTED Semaev system {S_{m+1}, prod_{s in S}(x_i - s)} as |S| grows, for interval, multiplicative-coset and random S.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Semaev polynomials (coordinate ring of E^m), the integer ordering of F_p, and the mu_3-stable choice of S available only for j=0.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The one genuinely unmeasured quantity in the whole prime-field-Semaev family, and the only outcome that could reopen the surface. The counting/structure half is already dead (measured structure ratio 0.6441 interval / 0.6428 random / 0.6433 beta-closed / 0.6940 mu_126, all matching the uniform-throw value (1-e^-t)/t to within 0.3%), so only the algebraic half is worth buying.
ranked.first_experiment: Install msolve (open-source, F4, builds from source). On a 20-bit curve with S_4 cached, form the ideal (S_4(x1,x2,x3,x_R), prod_{s in S}(x_i - s) for i=1..3) and sweep |S| over 20,40,60,80,100,120 for S = interval, S = mu_d coset, S = random control. Record msolve's maximum Macaulay degree and matrix dimension.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if d_reg/|S| converges to a positive constant (prediction: d_reg = Theta(|S|) with slope ~m, columns ~|S|^m, identically for all three families) — that confirms the minimal-vanishing-polynomial dichotomy and closes the algebraic route for EVERY S. ESCALATE immediately if d_reg is bounded or grows as o(|S|).
ranked.audit_flag: For any S the unique minimal polynomial vanishing on it has degree exactly |S|, so either the solver pays degree |S| (worse than the N^{m-1} brute force) or S is not Zariski-closed and Groebner has zero purchase; the stated kill criterion (ratio > 1.2) is also forbidden by the idea's own counting cap.

ranked.title: Sub-birthday-on-a-class: a class x solver grid measured against the universal sqrt(n/delta) line
ranked.surface: Structured scalar classes (CM/ring-theoretic) x non-generic solvers
ranked.one_line: Build the referee: a group-operation-counting harness that reproduces exponent 0.500 for kangaroo, Gaudry-Schost and splitting systems, and that every future structured-scalar proposal must pass through.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The classes themselves are generic-subset DL (Shoup extends verbatim to a restricted exponent set); the non-genericity lives only in the solver column — F4 on summation systems, LLL small-root, bit-level SAT.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Not an attack but a scorer, and the program badly needs one: the sqrt(n/delta) accounting identity explains why every known structured-scalar speedup lands exactly at break-even, and a calibrated instrument stops the next six proposals from re-arguing it. Cheap, and the only reliable defence against the timeout-censoring false positives that the grid as originally specified would manufacture.
ranked.first_experiment: C harness on y^2=x^3+7 over prime-order p = 1 mod 3 at 24/28/32/36/40 bits measuring group-operation COUNTS (not wall clock) for (a) kangaroo on an interval of width W, (b) Gaudry-Schost on the Eisenstein ball {a+b*lambda : |a|,|b| < R}, (c) splitting-system search on low-weight k, each swept over 4-5 class sizes AT FIXED n so log T is fitted against log|C| within one curve.
ranked.kill_criteria: The harness is CORRECT only if all three give e = 0.500 +- 0.02 and the density-corrected total lands on sqrt(n/delta). Treat any measured e < 0.48 as an instrumentation bug (censored timeouts, miscounted |C| from collisions, toy-size artifact) until reproduced at two more bit sizes.
ranked.audit_flag: The k = a*b cell has density 0.64 at 256 bits, so |C| ~ n and the cell IS the target problem restated; and Cheon 2006 is a generic algorithm with a matching generic lower bound, so it is not a precedent for exponent structure defeating the generic model.

ranked.title: Eisenstein residue coordinates: Coppersmith-Odlyzko-Schroeppel smoothness transplanted, with beta as an exact lattice rotation
ranked.surface: Coordinate-field splitting p = pi*pibar in Z[omega] x Semaev / Coppersmith lattices
ranked.one_line: Replace the counting statistic rho_rel with a RANK-aware screen: build the actual relation matrix over F_n and report rank per unit work, which automatically discounts endomorphism-induced degeneracy.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The ring isomorphism F_p = Z[omega]/(pi) acting on the COORDINATE field rather than the group, so that beta and the unit omega are the same object: nu(beta*x)=nu(x) exactly (0 failures in 3000 trials), and for a=0 only, S_3(beta*x1,beta*x2,beta*x3) = beta*S_3 identically.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Its failure mode is the single most transferable lesson in the queue: a mu_3-stable factor base produces a large counting excess (rho_eis 3.5-4.7 vs interval 1.0-1.2) that is 67-75% the identity relation P + phi(P) + phi^2(P) = O and therefore rank zero. Any future factor-base shape stabilized by an endomorphism with 1+lambda+lambda^2=0 will fake the same signal, so rho_count must be retired in favour of rho_rank program-wide.
ranked.first_experiment: Generalize scratchpad/count2.py: (i) count decompositions of a random target, S_4(x1,x2,x3,x(R))=0, not S_3=0 among factor-base points; (ii) build the relation matrix over F_n and report rho_rank, not rho_count; (iii) sweep p from 2^20 to 2^32 with B = p^{1/3} and fit the exponent of log(rho_rank)/log(p).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if rho_rank -> 1 with no trend in p (nontrivial ratios already measured at 1.25, 1.28, 1.44, 1.25 vs interval 1.06, 1.16, 1.17, 0.80 — a constant, consistent with factor-3 orbit folding). A constant, however large, is dead; only a growing trend survives.
ranked.audit_flag: A box condition is archimedean so it cannot enter the ideal at all — the Groebner system for an Eisenstein box is bit-identical to the interval case; and a linear volume-preserving change of variables leaves the Coppersmith reach unchanged.

ranked.title: Dickson/torus factor base: the one intermediate-size ALGEBRAIC subset of F_p that secp256k1 admits
ranked.surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves
ranked.one_line: Measure whether sparsity survives elimination: compute Res_{x1}(f, x1^d - 1) for a polynomial of degree 4 per variable and count nonzero terms of the eliminant.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Field structure of F_p and F_{p^2} (norm-1 torus, Dickson/Lucas recurrences), the arithmetic of p+1 for this specific prime, and Semaev polynomials on top; 'x in S_d' is a genuine degree-d condition with an O(log d) straight-line membership test.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Two hours for a kill that needs no curve and no prime at all, and the measurement (eliminant density) generalises to every 'sparse algebraic constraint' proposal. Mostly already run: for m=2, Res(f, x^d-1) has degree exactly 4d and is fully dense (4d+1 terms for d=5,7,11,13,17,23); for m=3, bidegree exactly (4d,4d), 169/441/841 terms = (4d+1)^2 exactly.
ranked.first_experiment: (1) Reproduce and log the eliminant density using the 2-sparse binomial x^d - 1 (strictly sparser than Dickson, so a failure kills Dickson a fortiori), d = 3..40, recording degree and nonzero-term count per remaining variable. (2) Time the full constrained solve for m=3,4 on real S_4/S_5 over a 24-32 bit prime, five values of d spanning 2^8, via naive (m-1)-tuple enumeration vs resultant/msolve; fit alpha in log(time) = alpha log d. (3) Log relation yield against d^m/p as the control that forecloses the 'maybe the set was correlated' retreat.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD the moment step (1) shows density (it does). Predicted alpha = m-1 exactly, forced by output-size counting rather than heuristics, giving total cost d*(p/d) = p ~ 2^256.
ranked.audit_flag: The subfield condition x^q - x that makes Weil descent work is ADDITIVE and linearizes at zero degree cost; the Dickson condition is multiplicative and its degree d propagates into every eliminant. Also: the best divisor of p+1 is 2^49.5, not the 2^51.2 needed.

ranked.title: Does any p-shape-derived subset or low-degree map on E(F_p) have abnormal bias?
ranked.surface: 4(b)/4(c) whether digit or fast-reduction structure is visible group-theoretically
ranked.one_line: Measure argmax STABILITY, not peak magnitude, and run the matched pseudo-Mersenne vs random-prime contrast that is the only genuinely novel claim in the family.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The base-2^32 digit representation induced by p = f(2^32) and the Solinas fast-reduction self-map x -> (x mod 2^256) + (2^32 + 977)*(x >> 256); SNFS-easiness of F_p^* is claimed but is not actually specific to this p.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Only a PREDICTABLE bias location is exploitable at 256 bits, and argmax stability tests exactly that at negligible cost. Already partially run: over six 16-bit primes the digit-box ratios 3.70-4.43 sit inside the random (3.74-4.54) and interval (3.85-4.46) bands, with argmax at 0.1835n, 0.3538n, 0.3603n, 0.4570n, 0.0537n, 0.3217n — uniform noise. The p-shape contrast subsumes the fourier-heavy-hunt proposal.
ranked.first_experiment: In C at 24 bits over 8-16 primes: (a) repeat the argmax-stability run; (b) build the Solinas fast-reduction ORBIT set, which is claimed in the write-up but absent from the code and is the whole of surface 4(c); (c) the matched contrast — ~30 pseudo-Mersenne p = 2^m - 2^s - c and ~30 random primes of the same bit length (m = 20-24), both with p = 1 mod 3 and prime curve order, two-sample test the parity-corrected max-statistic distributions.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if the two prime families are indistinguishable (predicted p > 0.3) and argmax scatters uniformly. Report z-scores against matched random controls, never a bare threshold: max|F|^2/N is Gumbel with mean ~ln N, so a naive 4-sigma rule fires on every run. Drop the degree-<=3 rational-map multiplicative-correlation sweep — gcd(n,p-1)=1 settles it a priori.
ranked.audit_flag: Kohel-Shparlinski-type bounds on sums over x(kP) are UNIFORM IN THE FREQUENCY, so concentrating the digit box's Fourier support buys nothing; and the claimed exploitation path via HNP does not exist (HNP needs a known algebraic relation, not a noisy homomorphism).

ranked.title: A multiplicative character of k would buy sqrt(n/d): audit every free predicate
ranked.surface: 8(b) free partial information + 8(e) Cheon-style auxiliary data
ranked.one_line: Measure the EXACT normalized correlation sqrt(n)*|S(f,chi_q)| between coordinate features and a multiplicative character of k, using the mu_6 vanishing theorem as a built-in correctness oracle.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: DL in (Z/n)^* is routine and DL in F_p^* is routine; the question is whether coordinates leak a multiplicative character of k — a feature class the repo's existing bit/residue battery provably never tested.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Carries a free, exact positive control that no other statistical experiment in the queue has: the mu_6 theorem forces S = 0 to machine precision (measured 3.6e-17 and 9.7e-17 against a 1.4e-2 noise floor) unless chi_q(lambda)*psi(beta) = 1, so a harness that does not reproduce that has a bug. Given the program's history of self-caught statistics bugs, this is the cheapest correctness check available.
ranked.first_experiment: In C, enumerate ALL k on 20/24/28/32-bit curves and compute S(f,q) = |(1/n) sum_k chi_q(k) F(x(kP))| exactly for chi_q(k) = k^{(n-1)/q} and F an additive character of each existing coordinate feature. Report sqrt(n)*|S| (null O(1), no drift). Use q=3 (free: gen_curves.gp already forces n = 1 mod 3) and add a filter for a second small prime factor of n-1 to get q > 3.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if sqrt(n)*|S| < 5 for every (f,q) at all four sizes with no upward trend. A usable leak means |S| = Theta(1), i.e. sqrt(n)|S| growing like sqrt(n). Report the one resonant (q=3, psi) pair separately — it is worth d=3, strictly less than the sqrt(6) rho already banks.
ranked.audit_flag: The antecedent is far stronger than the consequent: a predicate returning chi_q(k) also returns chi_q(k+j) and chi_q(tk) for free, so O(log n / log q) shifted values determine k outright — the payoff is not sqrt(n/d), it is a full break, which makes the hypothesis correspondingly unlikely.

ranked.title: Can a LEARNED advice string beat the generic ST^2 = Theta(n) preprocessing trade-off?
ranked.surface: 7d ML as a lossy compressor, measured against a tight generic bound
ranked.one_line: Measure exact mutual information between ~200 cheap coordinate features and the top bits of k over the WHOLE group, with a permutation null and Bonferroni.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Advice computed from, and online queries against, the explicit coordinate representation — bit patterns of x(kP), Legendre symbols, x mod small primes, lambda-orbit invariants.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Two hours, exact (no sampling noise, because you hold the whole group), and by Blum-Micali self-correction a single measured bit of advantage is already a full DLP solver — so you never need to build the kangaroo fallback, price model evaluation, or fit a slope. It is the cleanest statement in the program of why 'ML for DLP' work has no baseline.
ranked.first_experiment: Enumerate k -> (x(kP), y(kP)) for all k on 20/22/24-bit curves. For f in {Legendre(x), Legendre(y), x mod q for the first 50 primes, each of the low 16 and top 16 bits of x, x^3 mod q}, build exact contingency tables against bucket(k) = top j bits for j = 1,2,4,8. Report exact MI in bits and chi-square, with the null calibrated by 100 random permutations of k. Pre-register the feature list; re-run survivors on a second base point.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if max z < 4 after Bonferroni at all three sizes, and if any feature exceeding the null has its z SHRINK as b grows (true structure persists; finite-size artifacts shrink).
ranked.audit_flag: The proposed slope fit is impossible by arithmetic: at b=20, S=2^18 bits the classical table runs T ~ 13 group ops while a 2^18-bit model costs ~2^11 group-op-equivalents per forward pass, so the ML arm loses by ~150x at every point even with a perfect oracle; and the lambda-orbit symmetric functions are literally e1=e2=0, e3=x^3.

ranked.title: Recover the DL as the cotangent scalar alpha mod pi (the other half of the Eisenstein CRT)
ranked.surface: 3 (j=0 / CM by Z[omega]); coordinate-side realization of End(E) = Z[omega]
ranked.one_line: Prove and log that alpha mod pi is not a function of the instance: compute gcd(n mod p, (beta-lambda) mod p, p) and confirm the fibre surjects onto all of F_p.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Two ring maps out of Z[omega] — reduction mod (pi-1) (the group action a generic algorithm sees) and reduction mod pi (the action on the cotangent space, where omega acts by the explicit constant beta in F_p).
ranked.why_ranked_here: An afternoon that yields a clean, citable impossibility statement for the entire 'lift and read the differential' family: the cotangent scalar of the endomorphism realizing a DLP instance is not an invariant of the instance, and the canonical etale/formal splitting of E~(Z/p^m) is computable in O(log p) group operations without the discrete log. That retires the family rather than one member.
ranked.first_experiment: Three short scripts (audit2.py, audit3.py already exist). A: print pi*1.5*n/p per curve against the observed candidate count (got 4.710-4.712 vs reported mean 4.7 / max 6 — the recovery statistic is the Gaussian heuristic and carries zero information). B: build s = [p * (p^{-1} mod n)] o naive_Hensel_lift in projective coordinates over Z/p^2 and assert it is a homomorphism, reduces to P, is invariant under relifting, and is equivariant. C: compute g = gcd(n mod p, (beta-lambda) mod p, p) and confirm g = 1 on all five curves (a 121x121 window already gives 14641 distinct c for one fixed (P,Q)).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD when C returns g = 1 — no functional F(P,Q) = alpha mod pi can exist, which retires the proposed 'null battery' before it is built. Do not run the null battery or the E~(Z/p^m) splitting test; both are settled.
ranked.audit_flag: c is pinned only by the archimedean shortest-vector convention, i.e. a rounding operation on a lattice coset you cannot form without already knowing k — so 'compute c' is DLP restated, in a form maximally hostile to the Coppersmith/p-adic tools it hoped to unlock.

ranked.title: Functional-graph anomalies of Lattes walks on the Kummer line
ranked.surface: 8(c) arithmetic dynamics + 8(g) non-generic rho walk
ranked.one_line: Measure group operations per INFORMATIVE collision (tracking the exponent 2-vector) for mixed Lattes/adding walks, and fit the exponent against 0.5.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: phi_m is a rational map on the coordinate line computed with x-only arithmetic; lambda is a single field multiplication; cycle structure is governed by multiplicative orders mod n, invisible to a generic algorithm.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked here not for its prospects but because it is the cleanest demonstration of a trap the whole rho surface shares: a 16-adding control with naive canonicalization gave mean rho length 51 against the random-map prediction 908 — an apparent 18x break that is entirely fruitless cycles returning identical exponent vectors. Under the originally stated kill criteria that control registers as a spectacular positive. The informative-collision metric is the fix and should be standard for every walk experiment.
ranked.first_experiment: Track the exponent 2-vector (a,b) for X = aP + bQ and score ONLY group operations per informative collision (b_i -/+ b_j != 0 mod n); log the fruitless fraction separately. Sweep frac_lattes in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0} with r=20 adding steps and a splitmix64 hash of the true x-coordinate, at 20/22/24/26 bits, with a BLS-style fruitless-cycle escape in the baseline. Fit log(ops per informative collision) vs log n with a CI.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD unless the fitted exponent is below 0.48 with fruitless fraction under 50% at every size. Do NOT report cyclic-node count or raw rho length — they decouple from collision usefulness by more than an order of magnitude in both directions (at frac=0.90: 3x fewer cyclic nodes than random yet LONGER mean rho).
ranked.audit_flag: The algebraically forced deviation runs the wrong way — phi_m cycles have length ord(m) = Theta(n) (measured 0.0625n to 0.25n at 20 bits vs sqrt(n) ~ 1025), so permutation steps make rho worse; and x-only pseudo-addition is 2-valued, so exponents cannot be tracked without y, voiding the claimed 5M-vs-11M constant-factor gain.

ranked.title: Leakage frontier: unknown scalar bits at which a bit-level solver beats kangaroo
ranked.surface: 7a, reframed as a scaling measurement in the partial-information setting
ranked.one_line: Measure the solver's per-unknown-bit growth exponent g against kangaroo's sqrt(2), and ablate URem vs a hand-written pseudo-Mersenne fold.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The solver reasons about the F_p multiplication and reduction circuit; with URem and a constant modulus, however, no information about p's shape reaches the clauses at all — which is precisely what the encoding ablation tests.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Two hours, and the only well-posed version of the 'does CDCL see the special prime' question. The crossover u* it was built to find is provably empty (60 s at u=8, timeout past 300 s at u=10 vs kangaroo's 0.3 microseconds, gap widening ~1.58x per bit forever), so the deliverable is the exponent and the encoding ablation, not a frontier.
ranked.first_experiment: Reduce the instance properly: pick k, fix the top b-u bits, form Q' = Q - k_hi*2^u*G in Python, encode only u ladder steps against base G. Sweep u = 4,6,8,10 at b in {16,24,32}, 5 targets per cell, 120 s cap; fit log T vs u per b; measure t_op from the repo's C rho core in the same harness. Then the ONLY well-posed p-shape ablation: same u-bit instance encoded twice, once with generic URem and once with t = lo + c*hi plus a conditional subtract; compare conflicts.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if fitted g >= 1.5 per bit at any b (kangaroo grows at 1.414, so only g < 1.414 is extrapolatable-past). DEAD for the special-prime channel if the fold gives < 2x conflict reduction. Drop the high-bits-vs-low-bits ablation and the HNP/lattice arm entirely — the former is a base-point change, the latter needs many samples and cannot be instantiated on one instance.
ranked.audit_flag: With the top b-u bits fixed the instance is EXACTLY a u-bit interval DLP against a translated base point, which kangaroo solves in 2*2^{u/2}; the solver loses at every u >= 1 for every b, so u*(b) is undefined rather than saturating.

ranked.title: Interval/GAP factor base + skewed multivariate Coppersmith on j=0 summation polynomials
ranked.surface: Index calculus over prime-field elliptic curves
ranked.one_line: Sweep the skew parameter a with X_1 = p^a, X_2 = p^{g-a} and produce the g_max-vs-a curve, a reusable constant for every lattice factor-base idea.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The Euclidean/lattice structure of an interval or GAP in F_p (invisible to a group oracle) plus the verified CM weighted-homogeneity of S_3 for y^2=x^3+b (weighted degree 4, wt x = 1, wt b = 3).
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked below coppersmith-crossing-exponent because it measures the same wall from a narrower angle, but the skew sweep is the one thing that idea does not produce, and the 30-minute analytic pre-check (Jochemsz-May E_1 = E_2 for permutation-invariant monomial sets) kills it for free before any code runs.
ranked.first_experiment: Spend 30 minutes first on the free analytic check: write prod_i X_i^{E_i} < p^{|S|} for S_3 and confirm E_1 = E_2 for every permutation-invariant monomial set, hence that achievable log_p(prod X) is skew-independent with ceiling 1/d. Then run the measurement anyway: PARI curve generation at 24/32/40/48 bits, x_R fixed at FULL size, Howgrave-Graham via qflll or fplll, sweep a in {0.1,...,0.9}, binary-search the largest g, >= 100 instances per (size, a), brute-force cross-check every root. One figure: g_max vs a, one curve per bit-size.
ranked.kill_criteria: Replace the originally stated criteria, which cannot fire (1/(2m) = 1/4 IS the m=2 asymptote, approached from below). DEAD if g_max plateaus below 0.6 across four sizes; DEAD if max_a g_max(a) - g_max(balanced) < 0.02; DEAD if the beta-dehomogenized lattice never exceeds the plain one. Do NOT build the m=3 / S_4 arm.
ranked.audit_flag: deg_{x_i} S_{m+1} = 2^{m-1} for every i, so the Newton polytope is a symmetric box and the determinant condition depends on the boxes only via prod_i X_i — skew is provably neutral; and the Z/3 quotient saves a factor 3, not 2^{m-1}, because beta does not preserve 'x lies in a short interval'.

ranked.title: mu_6-invariant regrading of Semaev systems and measured first-fall degree over a prime field
ranked.surface: 2(b) j=0/lambda extra structure + 2(d) symmetry reduction
ranked.one_line: Measure the degree of first rank fall for {S_{m+1}, f_V(x_i)} in raw vs mu_3-invariant encodings and fit it against log p.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The j=0 automorphism acting on x by x -> beta*x with beta^3 = 1 in F_p, plus the weighted grading of the Weierstrass model; verified symbolically that S_3(x, beta x, beta^2 x) = 0 identically.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Its symmetry half is already settled analytically at zero cost (the mu_3-invariant block is exactly 1/3 of the monomials: 4845 -> 1596 at m=4/D=16, ratio 3.036; 20349 -> 6657 at m=5, ratio 3.057), which fires the '<6x' kill criterion on paper. The remaining first-fall measurement is worth a few hours because it is the reusable quantity for the whole 2(b)/2(d) prime-field-Semaev surface, not just this idea.
ranked.first_experiment: Zero-cost: log the 1/3 monomial-block counts for m=3,4,5. Then at p = 2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^18 on y^2 = x^3+7 with prime order, m = 2 and 3, factor base V a random mu_3-stable subset of size ceil(p^{1/m}): build {S_{m+1}(x_1..x_m,x_R), f_V(x_i)} and measure the degree of first rank fall with a hand-rolled graded Macaulay rank over F_p (numpy mod-p elimination to degree ~40) in both encodings; fit deg_ff vs log p.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if deg_ff ~ m(|V|-1) ~ p^{1/m}, i.e. grows polynomially in p, identically in both encodings up to the factor-3 column count. Only a deg_ff bounded as p grows reopens anything, and that should be triple-checked for a bug in the factor-base construction before being believed. Abandon if it exceeds one working day.
ranked.audit_flag: [-1] acts trivially on x for every curve, so the baseline symmetry is S_m not {+-1} x S_m; quotienting by a finite group of order 3 cannot remove a variable; and the real system with x_R fixed is not mu_3-invariant at all, since the action sends the system for R to the system for lambda*R.

ranked.title: Scalar multiplication as an arithmetization-oriented cipher whose rounds commute
ranked.surface: Algebraic cryptanalysis of the iterated ladder circuit over F_p
ranked.one_line: Measure the multilinear ANF density and degree of the map from r unknown scalar bits to x(kG) — the cheapest possible gate on every algebraic-ladder proposal.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The explicit arithmetization of the group law: scalar multiplication as a fixed low-degree F_p system with ~3 unknowns per round, with lambda supplying a second equation direction.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The density gate costs minutes and dominates any F4 runtime fit: measured 100% dense at maximal degree r for r = 8,10,12,14 at p = 615799 and p = 2895943 (16384/16384 nonzero coefficients at r=14). It is the right instrument for this idea AND for theta-hadamard-round-inversion, and it is the only step that would justify buying msolve time on ladder systems.
ranked.first_experiment: Rerun scratchpad/anf.py at r up to 20 on three or four 20-32 bit curves, and extend it to unknown HIGH bits and to a windowed/NAF recoding rather than only low bits. Reject anomalous curves in the search (my first random 20-bit j=0 curve had N = p = 1021417 and would have been trivially broken by Smart's attack, contaminating the measurement).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if density stays at 1.0 and degree at r — it does. Proceed to msolve only if density drops below ~0.9. If the F4 arm is ever run, the control must break the group law algebraically (a random quadratic of matching degree, or a cube map between rounds), never by affine conjugation.
ranked.audit_flag: The premise is false — R0(R1(m)) = 4m+2 vs R1(R0(m)) = 4m+1, so ladder rounds do not commute (they generate a metabelian affine monoid); and the proposed decisive ablation (conjugate each step by a random affine map) is an invertible change of coordinates that preserves the Hilbert function, so it is guaranteed to return 'no change' regardless of the hypothesis.

ranked.title: Local Tate duality as a discrete-log functional: ramified n-torsors over Q_p
ranked.surface: 5(a) making 'lift and measure' work when #E != p
ranked.one_line: Confirm the p-adic Tate pairing is trivial with correct normalization, then measure the cost of constructing the ramified class as a function of embedding degree.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Q_p itself: the canonical splitting E(Q_p) = Z_p (+) E(F_p) from gcd(n,p)=1, and the valuation giving Q_p^*/(Q_p^*)^n = Z/n unconditionally, with no embedding-degree condition — unlike F_p, where F_p^*/(F_p^*)^n is trivial when gcd(n,p-1)=1.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked here entirely for one finding that is worth more than the idea: evaluating f_{n,P} at the POINT Q instead of a degree-0 divisor returns 'NONTRIVIAL, valuation 1' in 30/30 trials — a completely spurious signal that would convince a careless experimenter the attack works. With the fix (D_Q = (Q+R) - (R)) the pairing is trivial 25/25. That trap must be logged prominently before anyone else runs a p-adic pairing experiment.
ranked.first_experiment: Reproduce the 25/25 triviality with correct normalization (ldrt3.gp). Then the diagnostic arm: search y^2 = x^3+7 toy curves for SMALL embedding degree d (d = 2,3,4,6 are reachable at j=0), explicitly build c = (tame character) tensor R with R generating the eigenvalue-p eigenline of E[n] over F_{p^d}, and CONFIRM <delta(P),c> equals the discrete log — a clean positive result proving the duality and the implementation. Then sweep d = 1..200 and plot the cost of constructing c.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD when that cost is Theta(d), which it must be since R lives in F_{p^d}. Delete the originally proposed step 4 (ramified base change over Q_p[pi]/(pi^d - p)): inv_L o res = [L:Q_p]*inv_{Q_p} = 0 for every d, so it is guaranteed trivial for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis and would be misread as precision loss.
ranked.audit_flag: The ramified classes are canonically supported on the Frobenius-eigenvalue-p eigenline of E[n], whose field of definition is F_{p^d} with d = ord_n(p) = the embedding degree — measured d = n/3, n/2, n/2 on the proposer's own toy curves. The embedding degree is relocated, not avoided.

ranked.title: Exhaustive census of low-degree relations among x(P), x(lambda P), x(cP), x(P+cG) on j=0 curves
ranked.surface: 7b automated conjecture discovery as a rank computation
ranked.one_line: Measure how the reachable multiplier set {a+b*lambda mod n} with N(a+b*omega) <= D covers Z/n as D grows — the positive-definiteness bound that closes the j=0-correspondence line.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: j=0 CM: End(E) = Z[omega] is rank 2 and the extra endomorphism is linear on x-coordinates, a statement about the coordinate ring and its correspondences.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The bivariate census itself is a theorem (bidegree = (N(alpha),1) with no translation, (2N(alpha),2) with one — reproduced at every entry: [c] gives (1,1),(4,1),(9,1); +cG gives (2,2) for c = 1,2,3,5,7,16, identically on a j != 0 control). The residual lattice-coverage measurement is the only part with information left, and it is the honest quantitative way to retire the family.
ranked.first_experiment: Enumerate lattice points alpha = a+b*omega with N(alpha) <= D and record how {a+b*lambda mod n} covers Z/n as D grows. Prediction: coverage Theta(D) out of n, so reaching scale n costs degree ~n, because the smallest alpha with a+b*lambda = c mod n has N(alpha) ~ n. Do NOT extend D to 40 or c to 16 in the bivariate setting.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD when coverage is confirmed Theta(D). Also fix the stated kill criterion before any rerun: the correct prediction is bidegree (N(alpha),1) or (2N(alpha),2), not the c^2 the write-up assumes — under the original criterion the mixed lambda-plus-translation family would report an apparent collapse from 256 to 2 that is just S_3, would validate on fresh points, and would be scored ALIVE.
ranked.audit_flag: For the family the idea calls its novel contribution, the bidegree is (2,2) for EVERY c — the third summation polynomial — and the relation's coefficients are polynomials in x(cG), so instantiating the 'cheap jump by c' requires first computing cG.

ranked.title: Xedni restricted to the CM/Mordell family: measure the lift density JKSST predicted, where the lift is canonical
ranked.surface: Index calculus by lifting to characteristic 0
ranked.one_line: Fit the exponent of the 2-point simultaneous-lift density against p and extend to 3 points, producing the quantitative JKSST replication specialized to j=0.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Lifting to characteristic 0 with j = 0 preserved, so the lifted curve automatically has CM by Z[omega] and stays in the one-parameter Mordell family y^2 = x^3 + k, k = 7 mod p.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The decisive measurement took under two minutes and already fired: rates 0.1088, 0.0921, 0.0456, 0.0191, 0.0124, 0.0051 at p = 1009..40009 with 1/(rate*p) flat at 0.0091, 0.0054, 0.0055, 0.0052, 0.0040, 0.0049 — a clean 1/p law. Extending it is hours and gives the deliverable the idea actually promised; the rest of the proposal should be deleted.
ranked.first_experiment: Extend scratchpad/lift2b.py to p up to 2^28 and fit log(rate) vs log(p); the claim to log is exponent 1.00 +- 0.03 with constant ~200 ~ the average divisor count of N = a1^3 - a2^3. Then m=3 prescribed points and confirm the exponent goes to 2. Optionally confirm that Lenstra's divisors-in-residue-classes algorithm makes each trial polynomial-time while leaving the trial COUNT at p^{1-o(1)}, closing the 'maybe there is an algebraic shortcut' door.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD at exponent 1 for m=2 (already met, and it is the idea's own stated criterion). DROP the rank-statistics test entirely (near-certain null: Selmer statistics are governed by small primes and the archimedean place, uncorrelated with a congruence mod one large prime). FIX the GLV-bias test: small-height global points' residues are automatically closed under +-lambda^i, so a naive KS test against uniform WILL report structure worth a factor of 6.
ranked.audit_flag: Narrowing to the Mordell family deletes the only cheap part of xedni: a plane cubic has 10 coefficients and point-incidence is linear, so ~9 points lift free; y^2=x^3+k has ONE coefficient, which incidence DETERMINES, so exactly one point is free and each additional one costs a full factor of p. Also E(Q) = {O} for y^2=x^3+7 exactly.

ranked.title: The (p/B)^g decomposition wall for covers over prime fields
ranked.surface: 6 transfer maps: covers into higher-genus Jacobians over F_p
ranked.one_line: Measure the slope of log(decomposable fraction) vs log(B/p) for the conorm image of E(F_p) in Jac(C)(F_p) and confirm it equals the genus.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Factor bases are sets of coordinates and decomposition is polynomial system solving; Aut(E) = mu_6 for j=0 lifts to any mu_3- or mu_6-equivariant cover.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Two to four hours of Cantor arithmetic for a clean quantitative statement — prime-field cover transfers cost Omega(p), the SQUARE of the rho bound — that closes surface 6's cover branch with a number. The relation-density argument is the binding one and is measurable directly without implementing any index calculus.
ranked.first_experiment: Pure Python with Cantor arithmetic, 20-24 bit p = 1 mod 3, E of prime order. (i) Take C: y^2 = z^9+7 (genus 4) and a genus-2 cover. (ii) Push ~10^5 random points of E(F_p) through the conorm into Jac(C)(F_p). (iii) For factor bases F_B = {points with z in S}, |S|/p in {2^-1..2^-6}, count what fraction of images are sums of <= g factor-base points by reading the Mumford polynomial's roots — no search needed. (iv) Fit the slope. Separately compute the zeta function via point counts over F_p..F_p^4 to check whether Jac(C) ~ E x A_3 splits.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if the slope is within 10% of g for g = 2 and 4. REVIVE only if the slope is < g-0.5 and stays below as p grows — that would mean the conorm image is anomalously concentrated on low-weight divisors. If the splitting check confirms Jac(C) ~ E x A_3, record that the cover is information-free and close mu_3/mu_6-equivariant covers entirely.
ranked.audit_flag: Relation density, not solving cost, binds: expected decomposable subgroup elements ~ p(B/p)^g forces B >= p to get B relations, so the floor is Omega(p) = p^{1/2} worse than rho for every g >= 2, regardless of any decomposition oracle. Do NOT run the proposed Groebner arm — over F_p a factor base of size B < p has no algebraic description below degree B.

ranked.title: Volcano depth from the CM conductor: thousands of small-degree F_p-isogenies as alternative encodings
ranked.surface: 3 isogeny class / volcano structure from 4p = t^2 + 3v^2
ranked.one_line: Measure whether the minimum rho cost over a full isogeny class is always attained at the j=0 crater vertex, on 10 brute-forceable toy classes.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The l-isogeny volcano depth at l equals v_l(v) where 4p = t^2 + 3v^2 — pure CM data. Transferring the DLP along an isogeny changes the coordinate encoding while preserving the abstract group, which a generic algorithm cannot do.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked here because the audit already produced two hard numbers worth logging as stand-alone negative results about secp256k1, and the remaining experiment is the only directly falsifiable form of the hypothesis. Verified: v = 3 * 79 * 349 * 2698097 * (91-bit prime), 4p - t^2 = 3v^2 exactly; the reachable class is 2^36.5 not 2^38 (Aut = mu_6 collapses kernels in orbits of 3); and the FEASIBLY reachable subset is only 2^15.2 = 36,762 curves, because the 2698097-layer needs kernel points over F_p^1349048.
ranked.first_experiment: On 10 toy curves of 24-40 bits, compute the full isogeny class by brute force over all (a,b) and confirm that the minimum empirical rho cost over the class is attained at the j = 0 crater vertex every time. Keep the Semaev S_3/S_4 decomposition-rate statistic as the only measurement not null by theorem.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if in all 10 toy classes the cheapest curve is the crater. DROP the min-height-of-j' test (j' is an element of F_p; 'height' is meaningless and only matters via lifting, which is xedni-dead) and the count of x < sqrt(p) (Weil forces sqrt(p) +- O(p^{1/4}) on every curve). FIX the kernel construction: precisely because l | v, Frobenius is a SCALAR on E[l], so there are no eigen-subgroups to separate — use roots of Phi_l(X, j(E)) in F_p plus Elkies kernel recovery.
ranked.audit_flag: Every non-generic ECDLP weakness known over F_p is a function of (p, n) alone and is therefore constant across the isogeny class; the only things that change under descending isogeny — End(E) shrinking from Z[omega], Aut collapsing from mu_6 to {+-1} — change strictly in the wrong direction.

ranked.title: Testing exponent sets for a holonomic vanishing polynomial
ranked.surface: Fast evaluation of structured products (EDS, elliptic nets, P-recursive sequences)
ranked.one_line: Run the validated Hermite-Pade guesser on the incomplete elliptic power sums s_j = sum_{k<B} x(kG)^j in the index j — a necessary condition for a short SLP, unlike holonomy in B.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The EDS/elliptic-net recursions: x(kG) = x1 - W_{k-1}W_{k+1}/W_k^2, so the vanishing polynomial is a product over terms of a highly structured recurrence; Shoup's model does not cover polynomial evaluation over F_p.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked in the expensive-but-live tier: the interval branch is now dead twice over (char-0 growth log(denominator) = Theta(B^3) vs the O(B log B) a P-recursive sequence allows, verified with log(den)/B^3 flat at ~0.49; plus an exact mod-p search at r=d=20 over 1600 terms on two curves finding nothing), but the Baur-Strassen shadow tests a NECESSARY condition for the prize rather than a sufficient condition for the booby prize.
ranked.first_experiment: Fix B = 2000 on a 24-32 bit toy curve, compute s_j = sum_{k<B} x(kG)^j for j = 0..1500 by brute force, and run the already-validated guesser (scratchpad/hol.py) on (s_j)_j in the index j, plus a search for an algebraic relation between s_j, s_{2j} and the curve invariants. ~20 lines on top of existing code. Keep BOTH controls permanently: the falling factorial (recovered instantly at r=d=1) and prod(x0-g^k) (no recurrence up to r=d=10 — if that ever reports structure you have a bug, not a discovery).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if no recurrence with r*d <= 400 in j on 20 curves and no doubling relation of bounded degree. A positive would be a genuinely new statement about incomplete elliptic sums and should be escalated immediately. One day total; stop if the power-sum axis is negative.
ranked.audit_flag: psi_m is polylog-evaluable because its root set is a SUBGROUP (it is an isogeny kernel polynomial, Velu plus decomposition); n is prime so E(F_p) has no nontrivial subgroups and F_S is never a kernel polynomial — the single known mechanism is unavailable by construction, and holonomic guessing structurally cannot detect the doubling recursion that would win.

ranked.title: The Lattes map as an SPN: algebraic inversion of Hadamard-then-squaring round structure
ranked.surface: Level-2 theta (Montgomery-type) model of the Kummer line
ranked.one_line: Run the entire harness first on the Lucas/Kummer-line-of-G_m analogue, which has the same claimed structure but a DLP the community has beaten on for decades.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: Riemann/theta identities and the factorization of the degree-4 Lattes map into a fixed F_p-linear map composed with squaring on G_m^2; the free move to F_{p^3} for rational 2-torsion.
ranked.why_ranked_here: The free reduction is the whole point and costs hours: V_{2k}=V_k^2-2, V_{2k+1}=V_k V_{k+1}-V_1 has squaring S-box, width <= 2, one additive mix and a conditional swap. If the solving degree grows there, nothing about j=0, CM, theta or F_{p^3} can rescue it, because none of that changes the round shape. Ranked low because the payoff needs msolve and the premise is already shaky.
ranked.first_experiment: Step 0, no curve/theta/extension: unroll r rounds of the Lucas ladder with r bit variables plus one state variable per cell per round, one quadratic per cell, b_i^2 = b_i and the output constraint; measure for r = 4,6,8,10,12,14 on 20-32 bit primes. Run the H = identity ablation FIRST — if it is not easy, the 'obstruction isolated to H' framing is falsified on day one for free. Record ideal degree and FGLM/lex-conversion time SEPARATELY from the F4 degree.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if D(r) or wall-clock grows with r on the G_m analogue. A saturating degrevlex solving degree on a near-triangular system is the expected FALSE POSITIVE; the real cost sits in the 2^r-degree elimination. Add a fourth ablation removing the conditional swap to separate round-algebra hardness from the 2^r bit search.
ranked.audit_flag: The premise is wrong about the ladder — only the doubling half is H o S o D o H o S; differential addition is a bilinear CROSS-multiplication plus a bit-dependent swap, which is where the 2^r entropy enters. And in the log domain every multiplicative operation is linear, so the hypothesis reduces to the Zech-logarithm obstruction, i.e. the hardness of DLP itself.

ranked.title: Z[omega]-indexed elliptic nets: the rank-2 exponent lattice as a substitute for descent
ranked.surface: 2(b) j=0/lambda pushed to the exponent side via elliptic divisibility sequences
ranked.one_line: Scale the variable count, not p: fix one curve, leave v bits unknown, and measure Macaulay degree and op-count against the 2^v brute-force and 2^{v/2} BSGS lines.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The EDS/net values W(k) in F_p are computable from division polynomials and are defined over Z; a generic-group algorithm cannot write the system down, which is precisely why Shoup does not formally forbid it.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked low but kept because the v-sweep is a genuinely diagnostic instrument (unlike the originally proposed 12-bit lever arm in p, which is worthless for Groebner asymptotics), and a 10-minute free precheck retires the novelty claim outright. Step 1 already verified: Ward's recurrence holds for all m in 3..40, q in 1..m, and x(kP) = x(P) - W(k-1)W(k+1)/W(k)^2 for all k tested at p=10477.
ranked.first_experiment: Free 10-minute version first: print log2|k1| + log2|k2| versus log2|k| and observe they are equal, retiring the GLV-halving premise. Then fix ONE curve at p ~ 2^28-2^32 with prime n, reveal all but v bits, unroll the double-and-add net chain (three W-unknowns plus a bit selector per step, d^2 - d = 0), ANCHOR THE GAUGE (pin W(1)=1 and W(2),W(3),W(4) to the curve — the a^{m^2-1} transformation preserves Ward but NOT the x-formula, so without this you inherit a spurious 1-parameter family and will misread the spurious-solution criterion). Sweep v = 4,6,8,10,12,14,16 recording max Macaulay degree, field-op count and solution count.
ranked.kill_criteria: KILL if max degree increases at all with v, or if op-count sits above the 2^{v/2} BSGS line. Honest prediction: degree ~ linear in v and cost near 2^{0.7-0.8 v}, strictly worse than rho.
ranked.cost_to_test: 2 days (needs a Groebner engine; gp has none and sympy will not finish)
ranked.audit_flag: |k1|,|k2| ~ sqrt(n) means log2|k1| + log2|k2| = log2(n), so two half-length chains have exactly the same total digit count as one full-length chain — the 'half as deep' premise is empty; and net RANK is the number of chosen points, not a property of the curve, so (P, lambda P) is a degenerate specialization carrying zero new information.

ranked.title: ECDLP as an Artin symbol: explicit class field theory of Q(omega) and elliptic units
ranked.surface: 8-wildcard: CM arithmetic of the global curve secp256k1 reduces from
ranked.one_line: Measure the height law of an index-d subgroup product of elliptic units versus a naive product, then test whether the d coset values are constructible in o(|H|) work.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: K(x(E[pi-1]))/K is abelian with Galois acting by SCALARS — a property no non-CM curve has (generic n-division fields have Galois GL_2(Z/n)) — so the discrete log literally is an Artin symbol.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked in the long-shot tier but kept because it is the only idea whose crux is a genuinely open computational question (fast evaluation of fixed-conductor subgroup products, i.e. Gauss-sum-type partial sums) rather than a settled one, and because the idea's own stated blocker is wrong in a way that matters: subgroup-product heights may well stay polylog by Kronecker/Stark, so the originally stated kill criterion would return SURVIVAL while the idea is dead for a different reason.
ranked.first_experiment: 20-26 bit y^2 = x^3+7 with prime n. (1) Enumerate the orbit x(jP) by repeated addition; lift canonically to Z/p^m by Hensel plus multiplication by p^{m-1}((p^{m-1})^{-1} mod n). (2) For each divisor d | n-1 with d in {2,3,4,6,8,12}, compute per coset the product over H of both a naive Prod(x(jQ) - x_0) and a genuine elliptic unit; fit log-height against |H| (predicted: naive linear, unit polylog). (3) THE CRUX: build the degree-d period polynomial whose roots are those coset values and test whether its coefficients are small and expressible as resultants/traces of division polynomials of size poly(log n).
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if step 3 finds no construction of the d coset values from objects of size poly(d, log n) — EVEN IF step 2 shows heights stay polylog. Only an empirical sub-|H| evaluation of a subgroup product keeps it alive, and at that point the interesting question is no longer ECDLP.
ranked.audit_flag: pi splits completely in K(x(E[pi-1])) (pi = 1 mod (pi-1)), so the Artin symbol at pi is TRIVIAL and the mod-p data contains exactly zero information about which of the (n-1)/6 primes above pi you are over; the achievable machinery gives full-group character sums (Katz p-adic L-values, k-independent) or conductor-direction norms, never a fixed-conductor subgroup product.

ranked.title: Sparse-limb factor base tuned to p = 2^256 - 2^32 - 977, attacked by bit-level constraint propagation
ranked.surface: 2(e) special shape of p + bit-level CP/SAT relation search
ranked.one_line: Fit the CNF solver's exponent against |S_w| on limb-aligned, non-aligned and random-dense primes — the control triple is what makes the result mean anything.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The pseudo-Mersenne shape of p makes reduction a shift-and-add costing almost no clauses, and the factor base is defined by the 2-adic digit pattern, a structure only this p has.
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked in the expensive tier because it is a full CNF build, but kept as the cheap independent check that the interval/GAP factor base is unsolvable by NON-lattice techniques — that is its real value, given that coppersmith-crossing-exponent only closes the lattice branch.
ranked.first_experiment: Pin the toy family properly: require limb width L with L | k, L | j, c < 2^L (verified non-empty: p = 2^24-2^8-29, 2^32-2^16-11, 2^40-2^24-173, 2^48-2^24-239, all = 1 mod 3). Pick b in y^2 = x^3 + b realizing the prime order via Cornacchia on 4p = a^2+27b^2 — do NOT insist on b=7, since the six sextic twists share an order multiset and b=7 will often not be the prime-order one. Start at m=2 (S_3), sweep |S_w| over 2^8..2^22 by varying k in {24,32,40,48,56,64}, fix the support pattern and iterate over C(k/L,w) patterns (do not encode an at-most-w cardinality constraint). Fit log(conflicts) vs log|S_w|.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD at slope 1.0 (= brute force for m=2). MANDATORY control: run the identical sweep on a random dense prime and on a NON-limb-aligned pseudo-Mersenne (e.g. 2^48 - 2^13 - c); if the aligned prime does not show a lower fitted exponent than both, the non-generic premise is falsified directly. Hard stop: if UNSAT certification fails within 100x brute force at the SECOND size point, record dead and do not climb.
ranked.audit_flag: Limb sparsity is preserved by shifts and addition and annihilated by multiplication; the cheap-reduction clauses are a vanishing fraction of the encoding while the dominant clauses are the multiplier, exactly where CDCL degenerates to search. Also internally inconsistent: 32-bit limbs give |S_1| = 2^35 or |S_2| = 2^68.8, never the 2^51 the complexity claim needs.

ranked.title: The wrong bar: for M simultaneous keys the target is sqrt(Mn), not sqrt(n)
ranked.surface: Coordinate/Semaev index calculus (instance-independent relation phase) x multi-instance economics
ranked.one_line: Measure probes-per-relation with and without mu_6 folding to confirm the CM structure is worth a constant 6, not an exponent, even in the amortized model.
ranked.nongeneric_structure: The factor base is a coordinate-defined subset of E(F_p), so the relation phase is a statement about the field representation; the log database folds by 6 under Aut(E).
ranked.why_ranked_here: Ranked last of the live ideas because the reframing is correct but buys sqrt(M) = 2^15 against a deficit of at least 2^113, so it cannot change any verdict. Kept only for the shared sub-measurement: the mu_6 folding ratio is the same quantity eisenstein-residue-coordinates and mu6-graded-semaev need, and the batch-model accounting is worth recording once so nobody re-derives it.
ranked.first_experiment: On y^2 = x^3 + 7 over p = 1 mod 3 at 24/28/32 bits, construct S_4 (and S_5 by resultant in PARI) and measure whether the mu_6/beta-scaling action on solutions does more than permute them in orbits of size <= 6: count distinct solution ORBITS with all x_i < B versus raw solutions, and test whether fixing an orbit representative eliminates a free variable — i.e. whether probes-per-relation drops by p^c for some c > 0 versus the predicted constant ~6. Log the empirical constant in B^m/(m! p) as a reusable byproduct.
ranked.kill_criteria: DEAD if the probes-per-relation ratio between folded and unfolded search is bounded by a constant (~6) across all three bit sizes — that kills every coordinate-factor-base sibling in the batch model too. Do NOT build the (B, M) frontier sweep: fitted brute-force exponents reproduce total ~ Theta(p) at every size and any 'crossing' at 24 bits is a small-constant artifact.
ranked.audit_flag: The reframing opens a 15-bit band (2^128-2^143) in a landscape whose plausible outcomes are 154 bits apart: with a free bounded-root primitive the single-instance cost is already 2^102 at m=4 (no batch argument needed), and with real methods it is 2^192 per relation, deficit 2^113.

top_pick_rationale: Rank 1 (coppersmith-crossing-exponent, Jochemsz-May residual) wins on every ranking criterion at once. (1) Information per cost: one hour of work against an already-built, already-validated harness, and it closes an entire branch — every interval, GAP, box, skewed-box, Eisenstein-ball, digit-box and sparse-limb factor base attacked by lattice small-root methods — rather than a single idea. Ranks 13, 21, 33 and parts of 5 and 11 all live or die on the number it produces. (2) Non-genericity: the lattice acts on coefficient vectors of an integer lift of S_{m+1} with the archimedean structure of Z; nothing here is a group-oracle query, and the auditor confirmed Shoup is not the binding constraint. (3) It carries a sharp pre-registered prediction (e* saturating at 0.20-0.25 against the e >= 1/2 that m=2 relation existence demands), so both outcomes are informative and neither can be argued away afterwards. (4) The supporting theory is already exact rather than heuristic: E(m) = 2^{m-2}(2^{m-1}+1)(2m-1) = 9, 50, 252, 1224, 6076 is a closed form, so E(m) > m is proved for all m rather than checked to m=8, and the naive-lattice measurement already sits at 1/E(2) = 0.11 to two digits at three bit sizes. The only caveat is that the naive-lattice threshold does not bound what SHIFTS can achieve — which is precisely the gap this hour of work closes, and the reason it is worth buying before anything else in the queue.
discarded: xedni-over-number-fields — provably dead and its experiment is a tautology: plane cubics form P^9 over ANY field, so a K-point is one K-linear = d rational conditions and the 9-point cap is base-change invariant; the only runnable check (matker returning dimension 10-r) confirms a definition, and the proposed rank study is computationally impossible (ellrank does not work over number fields, and the rescue via quadratic-twist decomposition applies only to curves defined over Q, which the construction's output is not).

mu6-symmetrized-summation — executed and closed: S_3 has 9/9 monomials and S_4 has 176/191 with some exponent not divisible by 3, so the claimed rewriting in u = x^3 does not exist; the solution set is stable only under the DIAGONAL mu_3 (60/60 relations preserved by the diagonal twist, 0/60 by a single-variable twist), giving a group of order 3, not 3^m. Repo commit 2ebcac5 already logged the graded version as negative.

mu3-character-gauss-sum-transfer — executed and closed: exhaustive max over all (a,b) at N = 2143, 4243, 7879, 11173 gives curve/sqrt(2n ln n) = 0.91, 0.90, 1.11, 0.96 against an i.i.d. control at 0.99, 1.01, 0.99, 0.99; |f_hat| is exactly constant on lambda-orbits (1.3e-13), so the entire CM signal is a 3-fold spectral redundancy already inside the sqrt(6) bar.

cubic-character-hecke-probe — executed and closed, and duplicated by the above: measured bias exponent alpha = 0.456 over N = 2^12..2^18, plus the exact theorem that chi_3(beta) != 1 (true for secp256k1, p = 7 mod 9) forces Sum_{Q} chi_3(x(Q)) = 0 identically with the three cubic classes exactly equidistributed. Jacobi sums attached to the Hecke character have modulus exactly sqrt(p), so the CM structure invoked as an escape is the theorem that proves square-root cancellation is tight.

u3-quadratic-phase — executed and closed: exhaustive max over all n^2 pairs (a,b) at four sizes sits at or below the i.i.d. random-sign baseline, and Weyl differencing plus Weil for curves proves delta <= O(n^{-1/4}) while extraction needs Omega(1/delta^2) >= Omega(n^{1/2}) queries, so no delta wins at any value. The proposed EDS/canonical-height source of quadratic phase cancels identically in x(kP) (a-exponent 2, b-exponent 0).

fp-log-quasihom — executed and closed: for fixed P and f in {x, y, x-x0, xy}, the number of distinct defect values is 0.625n, 0.623n, 0.625n at 14/17/20 bits, i.e. 1 - 1/e to two digits (a uniformly random map), and the degree bound (deg(f o tau_P) + deg f <= 4) makes the support Theta(n) by theorem. The 'computable from the representation' branch is trivially true and useless: delta is log_g of an explicit rational function, so its conditional entropy given the representation is zero.

ring-descent-splitting-wall — executed and closed: the canonical section sigma is a poly-time-computable group isomorphism whose inverse is reduction mod p (verified homomorphism, lift-independent, equivariant at k=2 and 3), so the lifted DLP is provably equivalent; the p-adic digit spectra are flat (max|F|/sqrt(N) = 3.09/3.26/3.81 at 14/16/18 bits against the random-phase baseline 3.07/3.28/3.50) and indistinguishable from the x(kP) mod p control.

canonical-lift-digits — executed and closed: since gcd(n,p)=1 both H^1 and H^2 vanish, so the 'unique primitive b' is identically h itself (averaging telescopes to -h exactly, verified 3/3), and h is not a polynomial in x^3 of degree <= 400 nor a rational function of bidegree (200,200) (0/40 fresh points). Its one useful residual — an anomalous-curve positive control — is already an arm of weak-family-positive-controls (rank 3).

eisenstein-ball-descent — executed and closed: the nontrivial excess is EXACTLY p-independent (18 at H^2=64 for p of 25, 27, 29, 31, 33 bits; 54 at H^2=256), so it is a finite set of global char-0 identities, and all of it is the universal endomorphism family {alpha, omega*alpha, x((1-lambda)P)} which becomes a zero row after the standard automorphism quotient. The exact/relaxed dichotomy is also airtight: |B| <~ p^{1/D} with D > m always, and the relaxed bound N(gamma) <= H^{2D}/p is satisfied automatically by every mod-p relation, hence carries zero bits.

weber-rayclass-height-wall — both kill criteria are theorems, so nothing is measured: Weber values of torsion have canonical height zero, so h(x(T)^3) <= 6*C_E is bounded independent of n by Silverman's height-difference bound, while the degree is exactly (n-1)/6 by class field theory and Gal acts simply transitively on the Weber orbits, so any separating equivariant invariant has full degree. Also unrunnable as specified: algdep on a degree-(n-1)/6 minimal polynomial is ~1365 at n=2^13 and ~700000 at n=2^22.

constant-provenance-audit — executed and its consequent is false: DLP difficulty is invariant under change of generator (log_G P = c^{-1} log_H P in O(log n)), so no property of G can encode a trapdoor. All checks ran and passed — rational reconstruction of Gx scores 0.551*sqrt(p) against a null median of 0.678; y^2=x^3+7/Q has conductor 21168, analytic rank 0, trivial torsion; n prime, n != p, ord(p mod n) > 1000, cofactor 1 — and the honest deliverable (the entropy-budget bound: p forced by the reduction shape, n computed not chosen, b worth ~2-3 bits) costs zero compute.

cheon-exponent-arithmetic-torsor — the pricing is already computed and the hunt is provably empty: n-1 = 2^6*3*149*631*p1*p2*p3 with log2 = 56.6, 67.2, 108.1, best d at log2 = 127.82 giving 2^65.00, but the cost is FLAT at 2^115.95 for every achievable d <= 2^56 (the largest divisor below the 56.6-bit prime is only 2^24.1). Every Kummer-quadratic selector rule is piecewise-affine in the exponent with 2 pieces, so Pr[psi(kG) = k^2 G] <= 4/n for the WHOLE family before any experiment (measured 1/8293, 2/8293, 0/8293 with Pr[affine] = 8290/8292). The oracle is also CDH, which has its own Omega(sqrt n) generic bound and, via Boneh-Lipton black-box fields, would give L_n(1/2) anyway.

point-to-class-group-map — provably dead by Lagrange with no measurement left: disc(Z[pi]) = -3v^2 with v 128 bits so h ~ 2^127 < n, and n prime with gcd(n, h) = 1 forces EVERY homomorphism E(F_p) -> Cl(O) to be constant. Independently, all three candidate maps depend only on x(R) = x(-R), so Psi(R)^2 = 1 and the image lies in Cl[2]; candidate (ii) is constant by definition since h(Z[omega]) = 1. The order-coprimality gate it would produce is one line and is folded into the surface-6 entries already ranked.

pila-zeta-encoding — executed and structurally void: the pipeline factors k -> Q -> zeta and the attacker already holds Q, so injectivity of k -> trace is free AND useless; the twist family dies by the exact identity a_{E^(d)} = chi(d)*a_E (verified for ALL k at p=8209), and the genus-2 family's a_1 is pseudorandom in k (corr(SB(k),SB(2k)) = -0.023, corr with k = -0.000, DFT max/mean = 4.28 flat), with the only detectable structure being the negation symmetry rho already exploits. Its one reusable asset, the equivariance test harness, is retained inside rank 27.

elliptic-net-2d-index-inversion — degenerate by the sigma-function identity: since lambda*P is a known multiple of P, W(u,v) = W_1D(u + v*ell) times an explicit quadratic-exponential factor, so the 'rank-2' net is a scaling-equivalent reindexing of the 1D EDS carrying zero extra information while adding one unknown. The GLV premise is also empty (Babai rounding on a 2^22 curve gives mean max(|u|,|v|) = 0.36*sqrt(n) over a box holding 2.2n lattice points, i.e. Theta(n) possibilities). Subsumed by zomega-elliptic-nets (rank 31).

lattes-centralizer-charp — census executed and the char-p loophole is closed in one line: psi = sigma o Frob^i with Frob commuting with phi_2 automatically, so the centralizer is Frobenius composed with the SEPARABLE centralizer, and Riemann-Hurwitz forces any char-p-only element to be wildly ramified with deg >= p ~ 2^256 (unevaluable at the 2^127.8 bar). Exhaustive search at p=7 (b=1,2,3) and p=13 (b=1,5) returned solution counts 3,0,3,3 — exactly #{alpha in Z[omega] : N(alpha)=d}/{+-1} — with zero exotic solutions and zero semiconjugacies to x^4 or T_4. The idea's own kill criterion ('extras bounded by an absolute constant') fires a priori.

cm-hermitian-self-pairing — killed by a counting argument plus a verified number: any self-pairing law f(kP)=f(P)^{k^2} forces the target's exponent to divide 2n, and the only constructible such groups are the MOV targets, but p^k != 1 mod n for every k <= 10^5 and gcd(n, p-1) = 1 exactly, so there is nowhere to land.
